newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India drifts easier in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India drifts easier in slow trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished mildly lower on Tuesday amid a continued lack of investor interest, traders said.

They said the market had drifted on thin volumes, with Reliance failing to track its local listing higher following selling of the stock on Monday. It is expected to announce a bonus share issue on Thursday.
"One of the market makers was hitting Reliance yesterday and the sentiment has spilt over," a broker said.
Traders said the market was consolidating following recent gains, and expected buying support to appear following any large declines.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.45 points lower at 87.46, a 0.51 percent fall, with the premium over the local market at 24.15 percent from 25.69 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index rose 30.19 points to 4,119.39.
Indian Hotels shed 0.67 cents to $23.50/24.50, SBI was 25 cents softer at $24.75/25.75 and Reliance was slightly firmer at $22.25/23.25. EIH shed 91 cents to $16.75/17.75 following results.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index closed down 0.66 points, or 0.86 percent, at 76.10 points, a premium of 38.89 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 1.04 points softer at 128.30, representing a discount to the local market of 3.07 percent.
